name: innernet
description: the memory your AI tools share — one versioned memory for every project and for you, read and written over MCP.

interface.shortDescription: innernet remembers your projects and who you are — every AI tool you use reads and writes the same living memory.
interface.longDescription:
your AI conversations keep starting from zero. innernet is the memory that ends that — a living context layer every AI tool reads from and writes to.

connect once, and this assistant already knows your projects: what you're building, what you decided last month and why, what's in motion right now. work produces decisions; innernet saves them back — versioned like code, so nothing you thought is ever lost, and every tool stays current.

what it does here:

- loads your context maps — each project is a structured, versioned map of its vision, roadmap, decisions, and state. open one and the conversation continues where every other tool left off.
- shows memory you can see — interactive views render your map inline: browse dimensions, read them in place, watch recent memory land.
- keeps a living checklist — each project carries tasks that advance themselves as work happens; tick them off right in the conversation.
- remembers you, carefully — a personal memory (voice, preferences, how you work) travels across every project, gated by disclosure levels you control. private stays private — enforced at read time, always.
- finds skills for the work — search innernet's public community, load a skill into this conversation, or keep a private attributed copy in your own memory. when you explicitly ask, innernet can also publish or withdraw a skill on the public community with its author, licence, and source attached.
- saves as you go — decisions and insight fold back into the map quietly, with a commit history you can walk.

innernet is platform-agnostic by design: the same memory serves ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Cursor, VS Code, and any MCP client. no lock-in — your ideas, versioned, yours.

innernet needs a free innernet.live account — sign in once and your memory follows you here. connecting, reading and saving are free; higher-volume plans are optional and sold only at innernet.live, never inside this conversation.
